graded_note: A6b, grade once - here, zero times. The source painting green-jelly.webp was itself ingested ungraded in phase AN3a (a colour elite: the grayscale grade would erase the green that is the whole read of a jelly), so these cells carry no grade either, and graded: false on the frame manifest says so. They match the static portrait they replace.

source: art-department/masters/enemies/green-jelly.sheet.png (2048x768 lossless master, 8 columns x 3 rows of 256px cells; see its own provenance.json, which records the rig that drew it), itself rigged from the shipped green-jelly.webp (torio's `Jelly A.png`, 2017-2018_added_monsters_ver5 pack, catalog slug `green-jelly`)
method: The rig keyed the painting's border-connected black ground to alpha and posed the whole jelly as one layer in 24 affine frames, every one of them about a pivot on its foot line (330, 548 in source pixels), so it squashes along the floor and stretches upward rather than about its middle. The master was cut into 24 lossless PNG cells by the splitter, row-major, then each cell was encoded to WebP q44 by the shared ingest recipe with the grade skipped. Every pixel descends from the shipped painting; the sheet master itself never enters this tree.
used_by: components/combat/encounter/CombatCombatantPane.tsx - the Act 1 elite in live combat
measured: A8, measured on these exact files: 24 cells, 179610 B (175.4 KB) in total, mean 7484 B, max 7920 B (green-jelly-21.webp, the attack's landing wobble), min 5122 B (green-jelly-08.webp, the struck flash) - against 12572 B for the static green-jelly.webp. 14.3x, +163.1 KB for one enemy. Beside the float-eye's 24 cells / 156452 B (152.8 KB): the jelly's cells are 256px like the float-eye's, and a little heavier because its painting fills more of each cell.
portrait_note: A7 (phase AN5a): the SHA-256 of the static portrait this set was drawn from. scripts/frame-set-portraits.test.mjs (root npm test) fails when the portrait's bytes no longer match: a swapped portrait retires this set (remove it or regenerate it from the new portrait).
